d: Exterior of the circus. At the rising of the tent the loud cries of praise, and prolonged beating of palms.
Alcandro, coming out of the circus in the greatest disorder, and furious with indignation, Hippia from the opposite side.
Sappho from the circus, that's it.
A multitude of young people, Lysimacus and sayings.

Apartments of Alcandro, attached to the temple of Apollo. Loggia at the bottom from which I glimpsed part of the beach of Lefkade. Climene surrounded by its Handmaids, intent on embellishing her with the wedding furnishings.

The steps of the altar, which burns before a simulacrum of Imeneus, are scattered with flowers. The calca of the People is immense; the sacred ministers surround the altar, near which are located the citarists and the other players, in all the pump of their gorgeous garments; then Alcandro from the piercings, followed by Faon and the Neo-Careers; finally Climene, among the hosts of the Conjoints and his Handmaids.
Sappho, surrounded by laurel and in pompous clothing, Lisimaco carrying the harp, and sayings.

A remote place near the priestly hostel. Alcandro is in the attitude of presenting Sappho to the college of the Arspesi, gathered near the anthro; she holds her forehead low and conserts her arms, as a humiliated and contrite person; Lisimaco stayed further back beside some Neomours: Hippia is among the Arspesi. I took a stretch of smell noise the wind.
Hippia, Arpesi, then Climene and sayings.

Less steep part amidst the ascent of the promontory of Leucade, of which I saw the top horribly protruding on the sea; here and there funeral monuments and triumphant columns of those who perished or survived the jump. The People Leukadius progresses full of consternation; then they proceed, accompanied by the sacred Guards, the Priests of Apollos and the Arspepis, among whom he is Sappho in white robe, and shining the hairs: Lisimacus mestamento follows her with the serpent and the lira.
